artifact_review: The Router identified a 'structural_collapse' in the console area (severity 3.0). I agree with this assessment; the area lacks the crisp geometric definition expected of a mechanical interface, appearing 'mushy' or melted into the shadows. This is a common AI artifact when rendering complex, small-scale mechanical details in low light. The 'texture_anomaly' in the background (severity 2.0) is also valid, showing painterly smearing inconsistent with the sharper foreground. The 'perspective_distortion' on the right carving (severity 1.5) is minor but noticeable. The Perceptual Quality Auditor's note on 'darken' supports the difficulty in resolving the console details, but the structural ambiguity remains an artifact.
alignment_reasoning: The image strongly aligns with the 'organ' class. The fine_grained_classifier confirmed the label with high confidence (logit 7.73). All testable visual checkpoints (pipe arrangement, silhouette, casing ornamentation, material reflectivity) are present and correct. The untestable checkpoints (console details) do not detract from alignment as they are physically obscured, not missing. The overall form factor is unmistakably a pipe organ.
artifact_reasoning: The primary defect is the structural collapse/melting in the console area (severity ~3), where the bench and keyboards fail to resolve into distinct rigid objects. Background textures show moderate smearing (severity ~2). While the main subject (pipes) is structurally sound, the failure in the functional interface area and background coherence prevents a higher artifact score. The scores are calibrated against Reference 2 (altar, artifact 3.0) which had similar lighting/complexity issues, but this image is slightly better defined in the main subject, hence a score near 2.9-3.0 is appropriate.
